entries.content: Finally got my refund after three weeks. Had to call back four times and reference my case number each time. The third rep actually escalated it properly to a supervisor who had authority to process it. Exhausting but eventually worked through official channels.

Was stuck in customer service limbo for two weeks with my laptop issue. Posted about my experience on Weibo and tagged their official account with my order number and photos. Got a DM within hours and they assigned a dedicated rep. The social media team has more authority to push things through than regular support.

Colleague mentioned that brands monitor social media mentions closely because public complaints affect their reputation metrics. When internal support stalls, a visible post creates accountability that phone calls don't. Companies often have separate social response teams with faster resolution authority.

Most companies have tiered support structures. Frontline agents handle routine issues while supervisors and retention specialists have broader authority for exceptions. Documenting interactions with dates, names, and reference numbers strengthens escalation requests.

Social media complaints are visible to potential customers, so companies prioritize them to protect brand image. Many brands have dedicated social response teams that can bypass standard queue times. A public post with specific details about your issue tends to get routed to staff with more decision-making power than typical call center representatives.
